result.markdown:
The best HR software for a small company depends on your employee numbers, location, and whether you need payroll included.

**My top recommendation for a small business is BambooHR for HR management, or Employment Hero if you're operating in Australia.**

If you're a small Australian company, I would shortlist the following\:

## Best HR software options

## My recommendation

For a small Australian company, I'd narrow it down to\:

| Your priority | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| All-in-one HR and payroll | Employment Hero |
| Professional HR management | BambooHR |
| Staff rostering and timesheets | Deputy |
| Budget-friendly HR | Zoho People |
| HR and IT automation | Rippling |


One important consideration: Australian payroll software should support STP Phase 2, superannuation obligations and applicable Modern Awards. search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2026 guide evaluates leading HR software for payroll, compliance, recruitment, onboarding, benefits, performance management, and employee administration. Gusto is named best overall for its full-service payroll, time tracking, benefits administration, compliance support, and HR guidance. Employment Hero is recommended for small and medium-sized businesses because of its customizable workflows, automation, AI assistant, and broad feature set, though advanced functions and add-ons can increase costs. Rippling is best for versatility, particularly for distributed teams, offering remote device management, tax registration, scalable services, and per-employee billing. Other recommendations include Remote Payroll for international enterprises, BambooHR as an all-in-one system, Zoho People for integrations, Breathe HR for simple employee management, Deel for powerful global HR capabilities, PeopleHR for mobile access, Paylocity for mid-sized businesses, Staffology Payroll for complex enterprise payroll, Workable for recruitment, and BrightHR for extensive workforce-management features. The guide advises selecting software according to company size and specific workflow needs, and explains that testing considered usability, features, security, support, pricing, and user feedback.
